chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn ash-Shah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamid narrated to us, saying: Abu Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimy narrated to us, on the authority of his father, saying: Anas ibn Muhammad Abu Malik narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said in his will to him:

O Ali! Usury is seventy parts, and the easiest of which is like a man marrying his mother in the Holy House of God. O Ali! A single dirham of usury is greater than seventy fornications, all of them with a close relative, in the Holy House of God.
ai.seo_question: What is the severity of usury compared to other major sins in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Kisāl*, this hadith from the Prophet to Ali (AS) establishes the vast spectrum of usury's severity, using hyperbolic comparisons to highlight its spiritual weight. By equating the lightest form of riba to marrying one’s mother in the Kaaba, and a single dirham to seventy acts of incest with close relatives in the Holy House, the text emphasizes that even small amounts of usury carry immense divine retribution. This comparison underscores the unique gravity of riba in Islamic jurisprudence, distinguishing it from other major sins through its quantitative and qualitative impact on the soul.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 24-8 Muhammad ibn Ali ibn ash-Shah narrated that Abu Hamid quoted Abu Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimy, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas ibn Muhammad Abu Malik, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his grandfather (MGB), on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB) that in his will to Ali (MGB) God’s Prophet (MGB) told him, “O Ali! Usury is of seventy parts. The punishment of the easiest of which is the same as punishment for committing incest with one’s own mother inside the Holy House of God. O Ali! A single Dirham of usury is more horrible in the sight of God than seventy times of committing incest inside the Holy House of God.”
